correctness.rationale: Each of four item allocations forces one of four valuation types into the smaller group and its antipode into the larger group; others are flexible. The antipodal-pair argument proves sufficiency if some count≤q and necessity otherwise. Pigeonhole gives universal cutoff. The exact infeasibility coefficient is the multinomial sum of four counts≥q+1; fixed-q asymptotics use binomial lower tails with pair intersections exponentially negligible; multinomial CLT yields the centered degenerate 4-variate Gaussian window. Direct original-definition exhaustive enumeration of 16,464 profile/group-size comparisons matched the count criterion; n8,q1 has 2520 infeasible among4^8, i.e.315/8192.
risks: Fixed group assignment, arbitrary item magnitudes, correlated or nonuniform sign profiles, or more than two items are outside result.
